title: Senior Engineer Hiring Playbook + 14-Day Onboarding Checklist
summary: A pragmatic playbook for hiring senior backend/infra/serving-runtime engineers (L4-L5): interviewer rubrics, panel templates, decision flow, and a focused 14-day onboarding checklist to accelerate ramp. This is a working doc for People Ops + Eng hiring managers; meant to be lean and actionable rather than prescriptive.
hiring_goals: Req: 2 Senior Backend/Serving engineers (L4-L5) — priority: serving-runtime team
Target close: 6–8 weeks from req approval
Interview bandwidth: 3 interview panels/week; calendar hold strategy for flexible panels
Diversity goal: ensure each finalist slate has at least 30% underrepresented candidates by sourcing stage
role_requirements: Core must-haves: 5+ years production systems experience, GPU/accelerated inference or distributed model serving exposure preferred, solid CS fundamentals (algorithms/concurrency), production debugging & incident experience, strong cross-team communication. Nice-to-have: quantization/low-precision inference, caching strategies, compilers or kernel-level optimization exposure.
interview_rubric: System Design (30%): defines clear trade-offs, latency/cost reasoning, stateful vs stateless design, scaling strategy, caching/KV management, fallback paths. Score guidance: 1=no coherent approach; 3=reasonable design with some trade-offs; 5=clear scalable design with operational concerns and failure modes considered.

Coding (20%): correctness, clarity, testing mindset, incremental improvements. Prefer short live coding tasks with emphasis on reasoning about performance and edge cases. Score guidance: 1=incorrect/unable; 3=passes tests but misses edge cases; 5=correct, idiomatic, efficient, testable.

Deep Technical Knowledge (20%): low-level inference concepts, memory/KV cache behavior, batching implications, quantization impacts. Score guidance: 1=surface-level; 3=solid with gaps; 5=expert with examples from production.

Behavioral & Collaboration (15%): ownership, communication, cross-team negotiation, shipping trade-offs. Look for concrete examples of trade-offs and stakeholder alignment. Score guidance: 1=poor examples; 3=good stories; 5=strong leadership and mentoring evidence.

Culture/Redwood Fit (15%): engineering judgement aligned with production-first mindset, emphasis on measurable outcomes and cost/performance tradeoffs. Score guidance: 1=mismatch; 3=aligns; 5=strong cultural add.
scoring_scale: Use a 1-5 numeric scale for each rubric category, then average weighted score. Pass threshold: weighted average >= 3.6 and no category below 2 (exceptions require hiring manager sign-off). Include short justification comments for any score <=2 or >=5.
sample_questions: Phone screen (30 min): Tell me about a production incident you debugged that involved model serving or GPU memory pressure. What were the root causes and mitigation?

System design (60 min): Design a multi-tenant LLM inference platform that supports low-latency streaming and can fall back to cheaper model variants under load. Walk through routing, KV/prefix caching, and rollout strategy.
Coding (45 min): Given a streaming token generator API, implement a thread-safe ring buffer for partial outputs and support cancellation. Focus on correctness and simple concurrency primitives.
Deep tech (45 min): Explain quantization trade-offs for generating coherent tokens at high throughput. How would you evaluate accuracy vs cost for a customer workload?
Behavioral (30 min): Describe a time you pushed back on a product request for being too costly at scale. How did you surface the trade-offs and what was the outcome?
panel_setup: Total loop: ~3–4 interviews, 4 hours max including breaks for on-site/virtual. Typical structure: 1x hiring manager (30–45m), 1x system design (60m), 1x coding or deep tech (45m), 1x cross-functional/culture (30m).
Interviewers: mix of senior IC + manager + product or SRE stakeholder when applicable. Avoid >2 interviewers from same subteam to reduce bias.
Calibration: all interviewers must read candidate resume + rubric 24 hours before loop. Drop-in panel calibration session weekly for hiring managers.
decision_process: Within 48 hours post-loop: interviewers submit scores and 3-sentence writeup via hiring form (link in linked_artifacts).
Hiring manager synthesizes feedback, runs calibration (if needed), and schedules panel debrief within 72 hours.
Offer checklist: reference checks, comp band approval, manager + recruiter alignment on start date, relocation/remote setup if applicable.
Fallback: if candidate borderline, consider homework ticket or second short deep-technical interview before final decision.
offer_signals: Strong system design depth with clear operational trade-offs
Multiple interviewers rate >=4 in technical categories
Clear examples of production impact and ownership
Cultural fit signals: pragmatic prioritization, ability to coach others
14_day_onboarding_checklist: Pre-day-0 (recruiter): send welcome packet, manager intro, first-week calendar templates, GitHub/SSO provisioning plan.
Day 0: manager 1:1 (orientation, mission, immediate priorities), HR admin tasks, accounts verified (email, slack, jira, git).
Day 1: team async intro, readme walk-through for serving-runtime repo, local dev environment checklist — aim for first local run by EOD.
Days 2-3: pairing sessions with buddy on small bugfix path through CI -> deploy flow; hands-on with local inference stack and KV/cache sim environment.
Day 4: shadow on-call rotation handover and runbook read; run through a simulated incident playbook with SRE buddy.
Day 5: owner-led walkthrough of observability dashboards (latency/token cost breakdown), cost reports, and common alerts.
Week 2 (Days 6-10): deliver a 1-day spike: evaluate a micro-optimisation (e.g., batch scheduling tweak) and present findings to the team.
Days 11-14: own a small non-prod PR from design -> review -> merge; run post-merge validation and write short retro notes. Schedule 30/60/90 goals with manager.
first_90_days_goals: 30d: local dev environment up; completed spike and documented learnings; clear 30/60/90 goals agreed with manager.
60d: owns a production-adjacent ticket; demonstrates measurable improvement (latency/cost/observability) or solid root-cause for a regression.
90d: independently owns an on-call rotation with solid runbook contributions; mentor a newer hire on a small area.
notes_and_tips: Keep interview loops practical — prefer 2 strong signals over 4 shallow screens.
For serving/runtime candidates, prioritize candidates who can reason about unit economics and failure modes (not just model accuracy).
